source: To prove (ii), first observe that the case where $P_0$ is free is evident, with no hypothesis on the ideal $I$. The general case, where $P_0$ is projective, is reduced to this by introducing a free $A_0$-module $L_0$ of which $P_0$ is a direct factor, and a free $A$-module $L$ such that $T(L)\simeq L_0$. The module $P_0$ is identified with the image of a projector $e_0:L_0\to L_0$, and it remains to see that there exists a projector $e:L\to L$ lifting $e_0$. This follows from Bourbaki, Commutative Algebra, Chap.~III, §4, no.~6, Lemma 2, applied to the sub-$A$-algebra $B$ of $\End(L)$ generated by an endomorphism of $L$ lifting $e_0$ (whose existence is ensured by (i)) and to the nilpotent ideal which is the trace on $B$ of the kernel of the canonical homomorphism $\End(L)\to\End(L_0)$. This proves the existence of $P$ in (ii). If moreover $P'$ is as in (ii), then the composite isomorphism $T(P)\simeq P_0\simeq T(P')$ comes, by (i), from a homomorphism $f:P\to P'$. Since $P$ and $P'$ are flat over $A$ and $T(f)$ is an isomorphism, it follows that $\operatorname{Gr}_I(f)$ is an isomorphism; hence $f$ is an isomorphism, since $I$ is nilpotent. This proves (ii).
